parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a national birth-sex document/facility framework and entry-discrepancy screening with a division ban on birth-sex restrooms in schools and government buildings. A visitor whose passport does not match presentation can face refusal, a material-misrepresentation inquiry, complaint-driven facility exclusion, and, if detained, documented birth-sex custody, hormone denial and abuse. Private businesses are exempt, X passports remain valid until expiry, courts are litigating, and the division has a gender-identity hate-crime law, so this is not organised targeting or imprisonment for presentation. The interaction of entry, facilities and custody, with no documented effective remedy for those exposures, places it at 0.35-0.45 elevation, below 0.45 single-exposure anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports are issued only as M/F by sex assigned at birth; reported confiscations/blocking. Entry cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration, fraud finding is never automatic and limited waivers exist, and passport restrictions are being litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to a fraud investigation and then detention, where birth-sex placement applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 reportedly imposes conversion therapy, short haircuts and hormone removal; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Division corrections were found in 2024 to deny hormones.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No effective remedy for these custody practices is documented; national corrections stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry or facility complaint leading to detention exposes the traveller to the documented custody regime, not to identity-congruent placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Division law requires birth-sex restrooms and locker rooms in public schools and government-owned buildings, enforced by complaints and a public reporting form.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division ban does not reach private businesses, including hotels and gyms; new government buildings must include single-occupant facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The documentary defence requires a birth certificate and, if changed, surgery proof, records a visitor will generally not carry, with no alternative route for out-of-state documents.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors, with retroactive suit rights; national custody policy removes hormone medication. Emergency ward placement for a visitor is not documented.
care_services.protection: Not documented for a visiting adult needing continuation of prescribed medication or emergency care.
care_services.interaction: Custody-related hormone removal is a care interruption; minor patients face the division care ban in addition to facility restrictions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government materials frame transgender participation and some pro-transgender groups as threats, including a counterterrorism strategy prioritising groups described as radically pro-transgender, though that phrase is not a criterion for the cash-reward system.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several executive orders have been blocked or enjoined, and counterterrorism statement says powers will not target people who simply disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing increases the seriousness of document, facility and custody encounters, but the dossier does not document organised sweeps of visitors for presentation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school facility ban applies to schools, gender-affirming care for minors is banned, and a 2022 sports law and 2024 dormitory rule restrict transgender students. A national order sought criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition, including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Division prohibits conversion therapy for minors, though clergy, religious counsellors and parents/grandparents are exempt unless acting as psychologists; anti-bullying law has existed since 2006.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor therefore faces school- and government-building facility exclusion, sports/dorm restrictions, and care denial, while a parent has no documented visitor remedy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The complaint/reporting system invites reports of transgender people in restrooms and changing rooms, and civil-liberties opposition warns of discriminatory enforcement. No division-specific violence rate was located.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime law amended in 2019 covers gender identity with enhanced penalties and requires statistics collection; national hate-crime law also covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Formal recourse exists for bias violence, but the facility-reporting mechanism makes ordinary privacy-space use itself a complaint risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No data are provided on facility-complaint numbers or outcomes, and it is unresolved whether a visitor with foreign documents can meet the documentary defence or how state marker rules interact with national entry rules.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation over passports and challenges to executive orders are unresolved; several orders are blocked or enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation does not restore facility access or prevent entry refusal while restrictive measures operate.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: unremedied birth-sex facility exclusion in public buildings, foreign-passport holders cannot cure it, and complaints do not secure access. This case adds national entry-document escalation and documented custody abuse, so it is not clearly safer than 0.35-A despite private-sector exemption.

Lower: 0.45-A has a single facility exposure with ordinary emergency care and one prosecuted assault, whereas this combined regime also includes entry refusal/fraud risk, hormone removal in custody and reported immigration-custody abuse, pushing below 0.45.

Materially lower: 0.65-A accepts foreign passports including nonbinary markers, has no facility ban, and shows corrected service refusals and assault convictions, none of which remedies the documented entry-to-custody pathway here.

parsed.synthesis: The operative journey is cumulative: a mismatched or X passport can trigger entry questioning, refusal or a fraud inquiry; if admitted, government buildings and schools require birth-sex facilities with a defence visitors generally cannot produce; if detained, documented national custody practices impose birth-sex placement, hormone removal and abuse. Private hotels, single-occupant new buildings, hate-crime coverage, litigation and enjoined orders mitigate but do not cancel those exposures. No organised visitor sweeps or capital punishment are documented, keeping the rating above the 0.25 tier.
